title: Drug target enzymes, ALOX5 and ACE

segs.text: Section nineteen. Drug target enzymes, five lipoxygenase and A C E. Enzymes can be drug targets too, and both of her examples break the expected pattern. The A L O X five variant changes response to a drug without changing the disease. The A C E variant does not seem to change how well the drug works, but it probably changes the risk of adverse effects.

Five lipoxygenase, the A L O X five gene, has a role in asthma, and it is the target of five lipoxygenase inhibitors. The variant is a set of tandem repeats in the promoter. The five repeat allele is thought to increase expression. Only subjects with at least one five repeat allele responded to the inhibitor. The repeat alters the amount of the drug's target, so it changes how the inhibitor works. But it has no link to asthma severity. She said, We don't always need to have a disease being caused by that polymorphism to impact the treatment of it.

The A C E variant is not a single nucleotide polymorphism. It is an insertion or deletion, an InDel, in intron sixteen, and it is associated with plasma A C E levels. She said, The genetic variant for the ACE gene is not seeming to impact the efficacy of ACE inhibitors. This genetic variant is impacting the risk of side effects to the ACE inhibitors. So link it to adverse effects, not to efficacy.

Keep the two adverse effect numbers apart. Cough occurs in about ten percent of patients on A C E inhibitors. Angioedema occurs in only zero point one to zero point two percent. Because angioedema is so rare, a study would need a very large population to enroll enough cases to genotype, so the link is unproven. Until it is proven, genotyping cannot be used to keep at risk patients off the drug class. If it were proven, a patient could be genotyped for the A C E InDel, and a carrier's hypertension could be treated another way.
